newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares gain, dealers cautious.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares gain, dealers cautious.

text.p: Latvian secondary list shares extended their modest gains on Thursday and dealers were cautiously optmistic about the struggling market's prospects.
Overall market volume was 65,000 lats compared to 71,000 lats on Wednesday and the Rietumu index inched up 0.61 percent to 192.70.
"The depression seems to be finished," said Viesturs Shterns, the head of the securities department at Unibanka.

Shares have been sliding steadily in low volume over the past few weeks in response to a spate of first quarter results which fell below market expectations as well as a general correction, dealers said.
But dealers say that bargain prices seem to be luring investors back to the market.
"Prices are very attractive right now," said one dealer.
On the secondary market, Valmiera Glassfibre bounced back, rising to 1.57 lats from 1.37 lats in trade of 6,400 lats after falling steeply on Wednesday.
Dealers said that its drop Wednesday was premature and sparked by one seller.
"Our market is very senstive to big orders," said one dealer.
Six other secondary list stocks rose and three lost ground while 14 were unchanged or not quoted.
The official list did not fare so well.
Unibanka, the Riga Transport Fleet and Kaija fish cannery all eased slightly while the Riga Shipyard and Staburadze confectionary rose.
Unibanka was the most active share in turnover of 17,000 lats and it lost five santimes to close at 3.55 lats.
